name: Eco Dedicated Server
description: Install the official Eco dedicated server through SteamCMD and run it natively in offline mode without exposing account credentials.
known_limitations: The server starts with Eco's fixed -offline mode because current online servers require an SLG user token or account credentials in process arguments, which GameNode intentionally does not accept or expose.
Eco clients must also be offline to join an offline Eco server; public server listing and normal online-client access are unavailable.
The default game and web ports are registered as fixed ports. GameNode does not yet edit Eco's generated Configs/Network.eco file.
The first start generates configuration and world data and can take a significant amount of time.
GameNode uses its bounded native terminate lifecycle; there is no reviewed Eco console shutdown command, and timeout escalation can force-kill the process.
Automatic updates, mod management, RCON management, and account authentication are outside this template.

config_files.description: Generated on first start; contains Eco network, listing, access, and remote-administration settings.

requirements.description: The reviewed Windows and Linux dedicated-server builds target 64-bit hosts.
Managed anonymous SteamCMD installation is required.
Linux hosts may need the libgdiplus system library required by the Eco server.
Ensure sufficient free storage for the server build, generated world, and backups.

help.summary: GameNode installs SteamCMD App ID 739590 and starts EcoServer directly with --nogui and -offline.
notes: The fixed offline launch avoids placing an SLG token, username, or password in process arguments.
Eco clients must be offline as well; this template is not suitable for a public Internet server.
GameNode reserves Eco's documented default UDP game port 3000 and TCP web port 3001.
On Linux, Eco documents SIGTERM as a save-and-shutdown signal; GameNode's bounded native terminate lifecycle may still escalate if the process does not exit.

findings.summary: GameNode does not place Eco SLG account credentials or user tokens in process arguments, so this template starts in offline mode only.
Eco's generated Network.eco file is documented but not modified by a compiled GameNode configuration adapter.
GameNode uses bounded native termination and may force-kill Eco if it does not exit before the timeout.

prerequisites: Network access to Steam content servers during installation
An amd64 Windows or Linux host
Offline Eco clients for local play
libgdiplus on Linux when required by the installed build
